sectors.note:
**TL;DR:** Robust market breadth anchors the daily trend as 5 of 11 sectors maintain "all-green" status, led by Energy and Technology, while Industrials ticks upward and Basic Materials slips.

US equity sectors exhibit solid underlying strength, with 5 of 11 groups classified as "all-green" (positive across the week, month, quarter, half-year, and YTD). Energy leads all sectors with a momentum score of 0.90, followed closely by Technology at 0.88. Technology also stands out as the sole sector showing sustained strength across 1-month, 3-month, and 6-month horizons. 

Sector rotation remains highly concentrated, with only two groups experiencing rank changes over the last 5 sessions. Industrials rose +1 spot to Rank 3 (momentum 0.65), while Basic Materials fell -1 spot to Rank 4 (momentum 0.50). Laggards remain firmly entrenched at the bottom, with Utilities (0.17) and Consumer Cyclical (0.18) showing no upward mobility.

## Strength
* **Broad Breadth:** 5 of 11 sectors—Energy, Technology, Financial, Industrials, and Healthcare—are "all-green," posting positive returns across all measured timeframes.
* **Top-Tier Leaders:** Energy (0.90 momentum) and Technology (0.88 momentum) command the highest momentum scores in the market.
* **Sustained Performance:** Technology remains the most consistent group, ranking in the top 3 across the 1-month, 3-month, and 6-month windows.

## Movers & Momentum
* **Industrials Advancing:** Industrials was the sole positive mover over the last 5 sessions, gaining +1 spot to reach Rank 3 with a momentum score of 0.65.
* **Basic Materials Slipping:** Basic Materials was the only sector to decline, dropping -1 spot to Rank 4 with a momentum score of 0.50.
* **Entrenched Laggards:** Utilities (0.17 momentum) and Consumer Cyclical (0.18 momentum) continue to anchor the bottom of the momentum rankings.

## Divergences
* **No Fragile Leaders:** No fragile "all-green" sectors were detected, indicating stable, uncontradicted upward trends among the five leading groups.
* **Wide Momentum Gap:** A steep divergence persists between top-tier leaders like Energy (0.90) and lagging sectors like Consumer Cyclical (0.18) and Communication Services (0.20), which failed to gain any rank ground.

rotation_phase.label: Late Cycle
rotation_phase.reasoning: Energy is the top momentum leader while Technology and Industrials remain strong and Healthcare lags, which aligns with a classic late-cycle market profile.

pulse.headline: Industrials rise and Basic Materials slip amid mixed sector momentum.

conviction.why: Conviction is medium due to a 45% all-green breadth, a mean rank agreement of 0.68, and zero divergences.

sectors.watchlist:
- Industrials - Watch for the sector to build on its recent shift in momentum, driven by an RS cross trigger. Confirmation occurs if the RS line holds above its moving average on a daily close, while a drop below the prior session's low will invalidate the trigger.
- Technology - Monitor for a sustained rotation into growth names following an RS cross trigger. Confirmation requires the sector ETF to clear its immediate overhead resistance on expanding volume, whereas a reversal of the RS line back into negative territory invalidates the setup.

risk_radar.relative_strength: Technology leads the market with a perfect rs_score of 1.00 and rs_confirmed of 1.00 (beating SPY on 6/7 timeframes), achieving both a new 20-session RS high and an RS cross. Energy also shows high nominal strength with an rs_score of 0.83 (beating SPY on 6/7 timeframes), while Industrials (rs_score 0.50, beating SPY on 4/7 timeframes) registered an RS cross.
risk_radar.risks:
* Energy exhibits a stark divergence between its high rs_score of 0.83 (beating SPY on 6/7 timeframes) and its low rs_confirmed of 0.28, pointing to a fragile, unconfirmed momentum profile.
* Both Industrials and Basic Materials show weak directional confirmation with rs_confirmed scores of 0.17, despite having moderate rs_scores of 0.50 and beating SPY on 4/7 timeframes.

industries.note:
**TL;DR:** Technology and energy maintain a firm grip on market leadership, while a severe rotation out of consumer discretionary sectors like luxury goods and department stores is underway.

Market breadth remains highly concentrated, with only 22 of 144 industry groups achieving "all-green" status across weekly, monthly, quarterly, semi-annual, and YTD horizons. Leadership is anchored by Computer Hardware (0.99 momentum) and Oil & Gas Refining & Marketing (0.98 momentum), both of which continue to show sustained strength alongside Electronics & Computer Distribution and Staffing & Employment Services.

A rapid rotation is visible under the surface. Financial and defensive groups are gaining ground, highlighted by a 20-spot jump in Asset Management and a 16-spot rise in Health Information Services. Conversely, consumer-facing industries are fading sharply, led by a massive 70-spot drop in Luxury Goods and a 28-spot decline in Department Stores. 

## Strength
* **Concentrated Leadership:** Only 15.3% of the market (22 of 144 groups) is "all-green" across all timeframes, heavily dominated by Computer Hardware (0.99 momentum) and Oil & Gas Refining & Marketing (0.98 momentum).
* **Sustained Performers:** Technology, energy, and employment groups show the most persistent strength across 1, 3, and 6-month horizons, specifically Electronics & Computer Distribution (0.89 momentum) and Staffing & Employment Services (0.81 momentum).
* **Broad Heavyweight Support:** Other notable all-green pillars include Semiconductor Equipment & Materials (0.83 momentum), Banks - Diversified (0.79 momentum), and Oil & Gas Integrated (0.79 momentum).

## Movers & Momentum
* **Top Gainers:** Asset Management led weekly gains, climbing 20 spots to rank 85 (0.63 momentum), followed closely by Health Information Services (+16 spots to rank 57) and Aerospace & Defense (+15 spots to rank 80).
* **Consumer Discretionary Retreat:** Luxury Goods collapsed by 70 spots to rank 112 (0.20 momentum), while Department Stores fell 28 spots to rank 113, and Apparel Retail declined 12 spots to rank 88.
* **Momentum Extremes:** Computer Hardware (0.991) and Oil & Gas Refining & Marketing (0.979) lead absolute momentum, while Advertising Agencies (0.063) and Airports & Air Services (0.057) remain anchored as the market's worst laggards.

## Divergences
* **Fading Leaders:** Several high-momentum groups are beginning to lose rank, including Metal Fabrication (0.75 momentum, -7 spots), Staffing & Employment Services (0.81 momentum, -3 spots), and REIT - Hotel & Motel (0.69 momentum, -3 spots).
* **Emerging Turnarounds:** Lower-momentum groups are quietly climbing the ranks, led by Discount Stores (+13 spots, 0.42 momentum), Telecom Services (+13 spots, 0.39 momentum), and Agricultural Inputs (+11 spots, 0.41 momentum).
* **Energy Divergence:** While refining and integrated oil remain all-green leaders, Oil & Gas Drilling is rapidly ascending (+13 spots to rank 9, 0.74 momentum) even as utility-adjacent groups like Regulated Water plunge (-30 spots to rank 104).

pulse.headline: Asset Management gains as Luxury Goods plunge amid weak industry breadth.

conviction.why: Low conviction is driven by a weak 15% all-green breadth, a 0.64 mean rank agreement, and five fading divergences.
